text:
noah.p: Hey all 1 new hire question. My first Buildkite run for redwood/api-proxy fails on the artifact upload with a 403 from the GitHub API. Pasting the tail log: 
```
Uploading artifacts...
POST https://uploads.github.com/repos/redwood/api-proxy/releases/444/assets -> 403 Forbidden
Error: resource requires authentication or insufficient scope
```

marco: Welcome Noah! Usually that means the token used by the publish step doesn't have repo scope or we swapped to the artifact-proxy service and the app needs reauthorizing. Did you fork the repo or run in the org?

noah.p: It's the org repo. I triggered the pipeline from a PR. I see BUILD_KUBE_AGENT in the job but no RELEASE_TOKEN env var.

ci-oncall-bot: Onboarding hint: do not create personal long-lived tokens. Request a scoped release-bot token from #eng-infra or use the release-operator service account.

ops-jen: Two quick things: (1) Check https://github.com/apps/buildkite/installations to confirm app install. (2) If the repo is private, our internal artifact-proxy requires the release token. I'll add a temp scoped bot token to the pipeline for you.

noah.p: Thanks, Jen. Where do I look to re-run only the publish step after adding the secret?

marco: In Buildkite UI click the failed job  Rebuild  "Rebuild from here" or re-run the pipeline. After adding SECRET_RELEASE_TOKEN (masked) to the pipeline env, re-run the failed step.

ops-jen: Temp token added as SECRET_RELEASE_TOKEN (masked). Re-run when ready.

noah.p: Re-ran and upload now returns 201 Created 389. All good. I'll follow up to swap in release-operator and update onboarding doc about artifact-proxy.

marco: Great. Follow-ups: eng-infra will provision long-lived release-operator identity, add a preflight check to fail early if SECRET_RELEASE_TOKEN missing, and note artifact-proxy in the new-hire checklist.

buildkite-bot: Build #9 (re-run) passed - step: upload-artifacts :white_check_mark:
